target_customer: Bloggers and subject experts wanting to publish short ebooks, and readers buying them
problem: Valuable expertise lives in blogs and minds but is hard to turn into books; traditional publishing pays low royalties and is slow.
business_model: Ebook publishing with revenue share to authors, ebook sales
product_category: Digital self-publishing and curated short ebooks

founders.name: Kevin Gao
founders.background_notes: Wrote a management consulting ebook in 2009 that, by 2011, earned more annually than most management consultants (per press at the time).

founders.name: Min Ming Lo
previous_startups: Earlier YC company acquired by Dropbox
founders.background_notes: Skills listed on YC page: engineering, design, product.

competitors.name: Amazon Kindle Singles
competitors.what: Short-form digital works program on Kindle

technical_complexity.rationale: Ebook production and storefront distribution through existing retailers required little engineering; the work was editorial and marketing.

defensibility.rationale: Author royalty terms and curation could be matched by Amazon or other self-publishing platforms, and content was not exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon already ran Kindle Singles and self-publishing tools; no acquisition of Hyperink found.

market_need_then: Press in 2011 described rapid ebook growth and bloggers wanting to monetize content; Hyperink offered authors up to 50 percent of earnings versus about 25 percent from many publishers.

branding.domain_note: Site listed as hyperinkpress.com (suffix 'press') rather than hyperink.com; acquisition details unknown.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Entrepreneur and Adweek in 2011; no merch or community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch press coverage in 2011 and a few well known author partners, but little sign of lasting brand recognition.

outcome_analysis: Hyperink launched in 2011 with a 1.2M USD seed from Andreessen Horowitz, SV Angel and others to turn blogs into short ebooks. YC lists it as Inactive and CB Insights labels it dead, but no shutdown announcement or cause was found, so the cause is not public. Easy replication by Amazon and low defensibility likely mattered, but that is unconfirmed.
notes: Funding total conflicts: 1.2M (TechCrunch Oct 2011, Entrepreneur), 1.22M (CB Insights), 1.3M (a later TechCrunch piece). The shutdown date and cause were not found; exit type follows the Inactive status. hyperinkpress.com returned HTTP 503. Ratings of defensibility and takeover risk are inferences from the product model and the Kindle Singles comparison, not from outcome sources.
